body.opens: The main store converted takes 5 min 54 s and 853 MB against the old store's 52 MB. Strata decodes JSON to find its way through its own index, and most of the late time is parsing; each tree node is JSON with keys escaped twice, and the attribute tree repeats the value tree. The author holds that the storage format should remedy this rather than caches, and that it is not to be postponed. Open: a binary layout read in place, and which trees to keep. Measured on this machine, Bun, the main store's 389 acts: the old format's reading 2.7 s in all, strata's offers 349 s, the store 853 MB in 903 blobs. Before nodes were cached, the first 100 acts read and parsed 460,827 tree nodes, 1.9 billion characters of JSON. A cache bounded by count, searched for its oldest entry on every insert, took 60% of the time; a Map slows with every entry deleted from it. A waiting layer's entries scanned one by one were quadratic; searched by halving, the first 75 acts fell from 15.4 s to 4.9 s. At act 164 the current trees were 112 MB, of which attribute 34.4, value 35.9, refers 25.5, ids 9.4 and words 6.6; keys 44 to 49 characters; an ids entry about 105 bytes, most of it its layer's 64-character hash. Over acts 201 to 240, layerOf took nearly all the time, and 73% of the profile was JSON parsing, its source not yet found.

name: Strata's format, for speed and size

body.opens: Every old head keeps its trees readable, so big rewrites leave near-full copies of the index: 395 of 507 MB of segments at act 164 were reached only by old heads. Open, the author's to weigh: keep them, keep a window, or one history index of facts stamped with their act, as Datomic does.

Next after strata: the reader's evaluate over stores, and judge, mint and land; then the interface and site over the new engine. Whether the old engine goes before the new one passes its 326 tests, or with the interface in one commit, is unsettled: the session kept it as the oracle, the author suggested the old can go first.
